description:
Flame in Freefall explores how fire behaves differently in microgravity using AI-powered analysis of combustion data.

Our concept turns flame behavior, temperature, and gas data into actionable fire-safety insights for future space missions.
summary: IGNITION.AI Pro is an AI-powered microgravity combustion and fire safety engine built on NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) datasets (BASS, Saffire, FLEX, SAME, and SoFIE). Using Python, TF-IDF semantic ranking, and non-linear flame spread physics, it helps mission planners predict spacecraft fire risks across oxygen, pressure, and ventilation regimes while translating orbital combustion insights into safer materials, clean engines, and smart smoke detectors on Earth.
details: What it does & How it works: IGNITION.AI Pro bridges microgravity combustion theory and practical spacecraft fire safety through three integrated modules: 1. SI Semantic Experiment Ranker: Built with Python and scikit-learn (TF-IDF Vectorization & Cosine Similarity), it indexes flagship NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) datasets (BASS, Saffire, FLEX, SAME, and SoFIE) so mission engineers can query complex scenarios in natural language and retrieve ranked experiments with critical Limiting Oxygen Index (LOI) thresholds and governing equations. 2. Microgravity Flammability Regime Simulator: Models non-linear spacecraft flame spread across oxygen concentration (14%–40%), cabin pressure (45–101.3 kPa), ventilation velocity (0–40 cm/s), and concurrent vs. opposed airflow—mapping radiative quenching (<1.5 cm/s), peak diffusion spread (5–18 cm/s), and convective blow-off (>25 cm/s) zones. 3. Theory-to-Earth Engineering Matrix: Translates orbital combustion findings into actionable terrestrial safety innovations with one-click CSV export. Benefits, Creativity & Intended Impact: By uniting NLP search with microgravity fluid-combustion physics (Gr → 0, Damköhler and Richardson scaling), IGNITION.AI Pro helps mission designers evaluate polymer flammability for ISS operations and Artemis lunar habitats (34% O2, 56.5 kPa) while advancing aviation fire-resistant textiles, low-emission engines, and multi-wavelength smart smoke detectors on Earth. Tools, Languages & Software Used: Python, Streamlit, scikit-learn, NumPy, Pandas, Plotly, Google Docs, and Google Slides.
